schema.name: time-profile
schema.documentation: When combined with other time-profile samples, creates a statistical picture of where your application is spending its time.

col.name: Sample Time
col.documentation: The trace relative timestamp of when the sample was taken.

col.name: Weight
col.documentation: The weight of a time profile sample indicates how much weight that sample contributes to the aggregate Profile detail view. The weight is a unit of time, but it does not represent a duration on the CPU. A sample has no duration, it's just a point in time, but they are given a fixed weight based on the sampling frequency in order to provide a context in the call tree, when a time range is selected. For example, if the same backtrace occurs in every sample for 1 second time selection, then when aggregated, that backtrace receives 1 second worth of weight. If the sampling frequency (determined by Instruments based on the system being profiled) was 1000Hz, then each sample is expected to have a weight of 1ms. It is imporant to understand that the code in the sample was not running for a full 1ms, as it's possible for millions of other instructions and stacks to come and go between samples. However, when aggregated over a long enough period of time, the profile of an application is tightly correlated with the actual behavior of the application.

col.name: Backtrace
col.documentation: The backtrace is extracted from the state of the thread's stack, at the time the sample is taken. By walking backwards from the current call frame to the previous call frame, and so on, Instruments builds a path from the threads current location back to the main function for that thread. Backtraces are useful for exploring the flow control of your application. They describe how the processor eventually arrived at the instruction currently running at the time the sample was taken (i.e. the value of the PC, or program counter, register). The PC value is always added to the top, furthest from the main function, of the backtrace in a time profile. The Profile detail view shows these backtraces combined together into a call tree, so you can see the areas of your code that are most often on the CPU, during the selected time interval, at least statically. That backtraces in the list view are the instantaneous snapshots at the time of the sample.
